title: Pear and Almond Tart
subtitle: Shortcrust pastry tart with almond cream and poached pear halves
excerpt: A buttery shortcrust case filled with almond frangipane and topped with halved pears. A classic of French and British baking that looks more demanding than it is.
sourceNotes: Pear frangipane tart is a staple of French patisserie, known as tarte Bourdaloue. Versions appear across Britain and France with various nut creams; the pear and almond pairing is the most enduring.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake a day ahead and store at room temperature. The pastry softens slightly overnight but the flavour improves.

content.text: Rest the pastry in the fridge before rolling; cold pastry is easier to handle and shrinks less in the oven.

items.prepNote: 100g cold and cubed for pastry; 50g softened for frangipane
blitzed to a fine meal in a food processor

content.text: For the pastry, blitz the flour and 100g cold butter in the food processor until it resembles fine crumbs. Add 1 egg and 1 to 2 tablespoons of cold water. Pulse until it just comes together.
Press into a disc. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Roll out the pastry on a lightly floured surface and line a 23cm tart tin. Trim the edges. Chill for 10 minutes.
Line the pastry with baking paper and fill with baking beans. Blind bake for 15 minutes. Remove the beans and paper. Bake for 5 more minutes until the base is dry.
For the frangipane, beat the 50g softened butter with the honey until pale. Beat in the remaining egg. Fold in the ground almonds until smooth.
Spread the frangipane evenly over the pastry base.
Arrange the pear halves cut-side down on top, pressing them gently into the frangipane.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until the frangipane is set and golden. Leave to cool for 20 minutes before slicing.

items.cause: Not chilled long enough before baking.
items.fix: Chill the lined tin for at least 20 minutes before adding beans.

items.symptom: Frangipane is still wet in the centre after 40 minutes.
items.cause: Pears released juice; oven temperature too low.
items.fix: Bake for 10 more minutes, covering edges with foil if browning.

items.symptom: Pastry is soggy on the base.
items.cause: Base was not properly blind baked.
items.fix: Return the empty case to the oven for 5 more minutes until it looks dry.
